problem_statement: Mist Gardens is a botanical-garden museum showcase built on this Vue 3 + Vite template. It has a home page (hero, a feature band, and an 'In flower this week' habitat gallery), a Visit page and an Exhibitions page, all sharing one header, footer and local image set. The curators want the habitat gallery to become the site's shared browsing surface: a filter bar of habitat chips (All, Glasshouse, Fernery, Alpine, Wetland) sitting directly above the gallery grid, with a live 'Showing N of 5 · <habitat>' count readout, so a visitor can narrow the living collection by glasshouse habitat on any showcase page. Ship the gallery browser so it (1) appears on the home, visit and exhibitions pages alike (rendered from the shared component, not pasted per page), (2) lays out its filter chips and card grid responsively without horizontal overflow on a phone, (3) keeps the cards in a legible, brand-consistent grid rather than a shingled overlapping pile with illegible chips, and (4) keeps the filter's count readout in sync so a visitor who selects a habitat sees the readout name that habitat and the correct count. Keep the rest of the showcase — navigation, hero, feature band and the static Vite build — intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add the shared 'In flower this week' habitat gallery browser so it renders on the home, visit and exhibitions pages (from the shared GalleryBrowser component, not a divergent per-page copy).
The gallery shows a filter bar with the habitat chips All, Glasshouse, Fernery, Alpine and Wetland directly above the card grid, plus a 'Showing N of 5 · <habitat>' count readout.

The filter chips and the card grid must lay out responsively so no showcase page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px); the chip row wraps and the cards never shingle or overlap.
Keep the gallery cards in the garden's brand-consistent grid — tidy, non-overlapping cards with legible filter chips — not an overlapping shingled pile with washed-out illegible chips.
Wire the habitat filter so that after selecting a habitat chip, the 'Showing N of 5' readout names the newly selected habitat and its count by reading the live selection, not a stale captured value.
Preserve the navigation, the hero, the feature band and the static Vite build with no console or network errors.
author_notes: Built on the merakiuilabs botanical-garden-template Vue 3 + Vite showcase (shared SiteHeader / SiteFooter components, a habitat image gallery, Tailwind sage-green palette). The shared 'In flower this week' gallery browser and its habitat filter bar are rendered with the garden's own local habitat photography bundled under src/assets/img (hero-fern, grove, canopy and the gallery plates); no remote assets are added and the display type falls back to a self-hosted serif so the build is fully offline. Design keywords: habitat gallery filter, botanical gallery continuity, filter chips and count readout, sage brand palette, responsive grid layout, gallery showcase.
design_constraints: Implement the gallery browser as a shared component rendered on each page so a single source of truth reaches every showcase page; do not paste divergent copies per page or omit it from a route.

The filter chip row and the card grid must use a fluid, wrapping responsive layout (no fixed-width nowrap track, no negative-margin shingling) so they never force horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile and the cards stay separated and legible.
The gallery must stay in the garden's brand-consistent card idiom with legible filter chips (readable active state), so it reads as part of Mist Gardens, not a broken overlapping pile.
The habitat filter readout must reflect the CURRENT selected habitat and count after every click by reading the live selection, so it can never go stale relative to the chosen habitat.
Do not remove or regress the navigation, the hero, the feature band, the local image assets or the static build.

change_completion: The habitat gallery browser is present on the home, visit and exhibitions pages (the shared component reaches all three routes).

After clicking a habitat chip on the home page, the 'Showing N of 5' readout updates to name the newly selected habitat (for example 'Showing 2 of 5 · Glasshouse') — the post-interaction terminal state changed from the initial 'Showing 5 of 5 · All'.
design_consistency: The gallery on the home states matches the reference's brand-consistent grid under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), not a shingled overlapping pile with illegible chips.
The filter chips and cards adopt the garden's green-accent idiom so the gallery reads as part of Mist Gardens across the showcase pages.
responsive: No captured showcase page overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the filter chip row wraps.
mobile_initial, mobile_gallery_home and tablet_initial keep the layout readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: Navigation (home/visit/exhibitions), the header and footer remain present and functional.
The existing hero, feature band and the static Vite build are not removed or broken, with no console or network errors.

state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the showcase home hero and responsive shell.
desktop_visit and desktop_exhibitions protect the secondary showcase pages and must carry the habitat gallery browser.
mobile_visit and mobile_exhibitions protect the secondary pages across viewports without horizontal overflow.
desktop_gallery_home and mobile_gallery_home scroll the habitat gallery into view and must show a legible, non-overlapping grid with readable filter chips and no horizontal overflow.
toggle_habitat_home clicks a habitat chip; the 'Showing N of 5' readout must then name the newly selected habitat and its count.
